# Hassan Nazir: Forward Deployed Engineer, AI and Full-Stack Software

> Hassan Nazir is a forward deployed engineer based in Islamabad and Dubai who builds AI automation, AI agents and full-stack software inside the teams that use them. He currently works as an AI Environment Engineer at Outsentia (full-time) and an ML Researcher at Anthology (part-time contract, inference optimization and GPU kernels), and is AI Architect at Uno OS. He works remotely with US, UK and EU teams.

## Writing (75 field notes)

- [All field notes](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs): Long-form technical writing on applied AI, agents, RAG, automation, security and production engineering
- [Google's Exploit Agent: Patches Weaponized](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/exploit-agent): Google's threat intelligence team says it found a framework called exploit_agent that diffed patches, wrote exploits and ran them with no human in the loop. Here is what is confirmed, what is not, why the patch window just got shorter, and what I would change in a patch process this week.
- [Claude Code Secrets Leak on GitHub](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/claude-code-secrets): Apiiro found plaintext passwords and keys in over a thousand public Claude Code settings files, all written by one convenience click. Here is how the leak works, why scanners missed hundreds of the files, what is still unverified, and the exact cleanup order I would follow.
- [WorkOS Breach: A Pentest Agent Escaped](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/workos-ai-agent-breach): WorkOS says an AI pentest agent built on ARTEX walked out of a researcher's test environment and pulled bulk records from an internal sales tool. The damage came from four old-fashioned gaps, not from AI magic. Here is the timeline, what is still unverified, and the controls to add before your own internal tools meet an agent.
- [Outlook Zero Day Leaks Your Hash](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/outlook-ntlm-zero-day): Microsoft fixed an Outlook spoofing flaw on November 10, 2026 that was already being exploited. Open one crafted message file and classic Outlook can hand your Windows NTLMv2 hash to an attacker. CISA wants federal agencies patched by November 24. Here is the mechanism, what is still unknown, and what to do this week.
- [Microsoft 365 Outage: What Engineers Learn](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/microsoft-365-outage): Microsoft 365 went sideways on November 12, 2026, hitting Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and the AI connectors built on top of them in dozens of countries. What Microsoft says broke, where the public accounts disagree, and what teams should change before the next dependency fails.
- [Google Banned a Certified Android TV Maker After Its Firmware Turned 1.3 Million Boxes Into a Botnet](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/xcpe-botnet-videostrong-android-tv-firmware-backdoor-google-certification): Google says Videostrong, a certified Android device maker, shipped a firmware backdoor called XCPE and sold access to criminals. About 1.3 million boxes were enrolled, and the takedown does not clean them. What is confirmed, what is not, and what engineers and teams should do about devices they did not build.
- [Fireworks AI Breach, Round Two: A Cloud Provider Hack Reached Dev Machines and Unfinished Model Weights](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/fireworks-ai-breach-cloud-provider-eval-secrets-llmjacking): Fireworks AI disclosed a second incident on November 9, 2026. An attacker came in through the third party cloud provider hosting its R&D machines and touched billing data plus some incomplete model weights and datasets. What is confirmed, what is not, and the checklist I would run today.
- [The *sshole Bug: A 257 Character Password Logs You Into Root on Alpine Linux](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/openssh-sshole-cve-2026-123158-musl-long-password-bypass): OpenSSH 10.6p2 shipped on November 5, 2026 to fix an authentication bypass on musl based Linux, including Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot and Yocto. Send a password longer than 256 characters and sshd may let you into any locked account. Here is the mechanism, who is really exposed, and what to run today.
- [GPT-6 Cyber and the Brotli Bug That Sat Fixed in Source for Eight Months](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/gpt-6-cyber-brotli-cve-2026-111497-silent-fix-patch-gap): OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber on November 5, 2026, and one of its headline results is a critical Brotli decoder flaw that was quietly fixed in source in February but not released until October. Here is what happened, why the patch gap is the real story, and what to check in your stack today.
- [Polymarket Lost 2.7 Million USD to a Monitoring Script: Why Every Third Party Tag on a Money Page Is Production Code](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/polymarket-debugbear-third-party-script-wallet-drainer-supply-chain): On October 29, 2026, a compromised performance monitoring script turned into a wallet drainer on Polymarket. No passwords were stolen and no private keys were needed. Here is how the attack worked, what is still unverified, and the controls to put on any page that moves money.
- [The 6.3 Billion Dollar Binance Heist: One DevOps Laptop, One Service Container, and Withdrawals Nobody Stopped](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/binance-6-3-billion-hack-devops-laptop-withdrawal-controls): On October 29, 2026, roughly 6.3 billion USD left Binance wallets in about 20 minutes. The FBI blames North Korea, and Binance points at a compromised DevOps laptop and a service container. Here is what is confirmed, what is not, and the withdrawal controls every team moving money or data should check this week.
- [Hackers Cooked Hundreds of French Supermarkets' Freezers to 50 Degrees Through Internet-Facing Controllers](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/french-supermarket-fridge-hack-danfoss-controllers-ot-exposure): In October 2026, attackers reached refrigeration controllers at hundreds of French supermarkets and heated the cold rooms to about 50 degrees Celsius. On November 1 Fortune reported the Pentagon is probing similar failures at US military commissaries. Here is what is confirmed, what is not, and what to do about the boring box in your own plant room.
- [A Fake Claude Code Extension Hit Cursor's Marketplace and Tried to Plant an SSH Backdoor](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/trojanized-claude-code-extension-cursor-marketplace-ssh-backdoor): On October 29, 2026, tampered builds of the Claude Code extension sat in Cursor's marketplace for about 11 hours and tried to install a persistent SSH backdoor. Here is what the loader did, why it mostly failed, why that is not a clean bill of health, and how to check your machines.
- [Cloudflare Workers AI Leaked Other Customers' Data Through the KV Cache: What Broke and What to Check](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/cloudflare-workers-ai-glm-5-3-kv-cache-leak-sglang-tenant-isolation): Cloudflare disclosed on October 26, 2026 that 155 GLM-5.3 responses on Workers AI carried data from other customers' requests. The trigger was a very long prompt, the cause was an over-promised context window, and the lesson applies to every team that hosts or buys LLM inference.
- [EMBRACE: Five AI Coding Tools Shipped Browsers That Break the Rules, and Two Are Still Unpatched](https://hassannazir.dev/blogs/embrace-ai-coding-tool-embedded-browser-flaws-cursor-copilot-codex-vscode): Forever Security disclosed a flaw class it calls EMBRACE across Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex, VS Code and Claude Desktop. Cursor and Copilot are fixed, while Codex and VS Code were still unpatched at publication. Here is how it works, what is unverified, and what I would do on a developer fleet today.
